 House prosecution: VP Sara bank accounts, undeclared balances remain unchallenged
 by 
 Jose Cielito Reganit
 Nov 12, 2026
 8:19 PM GMT+8
 STILL UNDISPUTED. House prosecution legal spokesperson and counsel Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr., House prosecutor Manila Rep. Joel Chua, and House prosecution spokesperson Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong (from left) lead a post-trial press briefing at the Senate in Pasay City on Thursday (Nov. 12, 2026). They said Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense has yet to dispute bank accounts and balances that formed part of the PHP817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth identified by forensic accounting expert Alexander Cabrera. (Screenshot from House livestream)
 MANILA – Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense has yet to dispute bank accounts and balances that formed part of the PHP817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth identified by forensic accounting expert Alexander Cabrera, House of Representatives prosecution spokesperson, Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong, said Thursday.
 Alonto Adiong said bank managers presented by the prosecution have already confirmed the existence of accounts belonging to Duterte, her husband, lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio, and companies where they held financial interests.
 He said some accounts contained balances not reflected in Duterte’s Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs).
 “So, that would be an indisputable fact because the bank managers themselves have testified on those bank accounts that bear or bore certain amounts,” Alonto Adiong said at a post-trial press briefing.
 He said Cabrera used the bank records and balances to determine the amounts allegedly missing from Duterte’s declared net worth.
 “At ’yun naman po ’yung kinuha ni Attorney Cabrera para po i-account kung magkano po ’yung hindi talaga naipakita sa SALN ni Vice President as part of her net worth (And that is what Attorney Cabrera used to account for how much was not actually declared in the Vice President's SALN as part of her net worth),” he added.
 House prosecution legal spokesperson and counsel Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr. said the records included year-end balances exceeding PHP20 million and PHP30 million in certain years.
 He said these amounts were among those considered in Cabrera’s calculation of at least PHP817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth and undeclared assets involving Duterte and Carpio from 2022 to 2025.
 Tolosa stressed that the defense had not challenged the authenticity of the bank accounts when the prosecution presented its evidence.
 “First of all, they did not question the authenticity of those bank accounts when we presented them,” he said.
 He also clarified that the bank representatives whom the defense later decided not to present were supposed to authenticate letters sent by Carpio, rather than challenge the account balances themselves.
 “Ang purpose lang na nakalagay doon (The purpose stated there was only) to authenticate some letters sent by Attorney Carpio regarding these accounts,” Tolosa said.
 He said the prosecution has yet to hear a defense witness deny the existence of the accounts or directly dispute the records.
 “So, to answer your question, so far, wala pa tayong nakitang testigo from them who will testify in this matter or sasabihin nilang hindi totoo ’yung account (So far, we have not seen any witness from them who will testify on this matter or say that the account is not true) or non-existent, to dispute it in any way,” Tolosa said.
 ‘Pandora’s box,’ floodgates of questions
 Meanwhile, House prosecutor Manila Rep. Joel Chua said presenting a Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) official to testify about Duterte’s possible dollar accounts could open a “Pandora’s box” and unleash questions her defense might struggle to answer.
 He said the defense’s decision to drop the bank official prevented further questioning about substantial transactions involving the BPI Julio Vargas branch.
 “Kumbaga parang magbubukas ng (It’s like opening a) Pandora’s box,” Chua said, noting that the prosecution could have pursued additional questions about the bank accounts had the defense presented the witness.
 Alonto Adiong said presenting the bank official could have opened a floodgate of questions about Duterte’s finances, including whether her alleged unexplained wealth exceeded the amount already identified by the prosecution.
 “Should they continue on or pursue presenting the BPI official, it would open up a floodgate of questions that they could not possibly manage,” he said.
 “So, I think that’s part of avoiding that flood, the opening of a floodgate, which I think the defense could not possibly manage.”
 He also raised the possibility that further examination of dollar accounts could reveal additional amounts requiring explanation.
 Cabrera earlier identified between PHP817.87 million and PHP1.5 billion in alleged unexplained wealth and undeclared assets involving Duterte and her husband.
 The defense has been expected to present a BPI official who reportedly brought documents concerning Duterte’s dollar account but later decided to dispense with his testimony.
 Chua acknowledged that the prosecution could only speculate as to why the defense withdrew the witness.
 “Well, we can only guess,” he said.
 He added that previous defense witnesses had faced difficult questions during cross-examination.
 The Senate impeachment court is hearing the defense’s evidence under Article II, the sole remaining impeachment charge against Duterte involving alleged unexplained wealth. (PNA)
